duplicate_pair_reviews.rationale: Broth retains 1600 ml cooking water; kornotto uses 850 ml and explicitly mashes beans to bind a thick dish without free broth.
Palt cooks pressed raw-potato dough for 35 minutes; kroppkakor use pre-cooked potato/egg dough and a 12-minute final simmer.
Chicken is enclosed between polenta layers and baked; lamb is pulled after long braising and served on loose polenta without final baking.
Loose toasted tortilla pieces are dressed immediately before serving; intact tortillas form a layered baked and cut casserole.
Bread is dissolved into a thick tomato porridge; the beef soup retains broth and serves bread separately.
Ravioli enclose filling in rolled thin pasta; bread-bean dumplings are a homogeneous soaked-bread mass cooked by steaming.
New salmon is chopped, bound and pan-fried as patties; existing full instructions bake intact salmon. Shared sides do not remove this main structural difference.

Both are the same simmered lentil/carrot breakfast structure. Bulgur changes grain texture but no sufficiently independent construction is established. Treat the two source variants as variants of the existing base; no import until bulgur requirements and complete variant review pass.

Both main components are bound beef mince shaped and pan-fried. Oval shape, egg binding, tomato sauce and rice are variants of the existing keftedes construction, not sufficient evidence of a new base. The existing oven method describes its potato side; its full meat instructions pan-fry the patties.

Both constructions cook noodles and raw animal input separately, then assemble noodles, raw vegetables and a sour peanut dressing. Salmon, different vegetables and peanut-butter dressing are ingredient variants, not an independently established main construction.
